name: Hand axe
summary: A hand axe (or handaxe or  Acheulean hand axe) is a prehistoric stone tool with two faces that is the longest-used tool in human history.

name: Adze
summary: An adze () or adz is an ancient and versatile cutting tool similar to an axe but with the cutting edge perpendicular to the handle rather than parallel.

name: Felling axe
summary: An axe (; sometimes spelled ax in American English; see spelling differences) is an implement that has been used for thousands of years to shape, split, and cut wood, to harvest timber, and as a weapon.

name: Broad axe
summary: A broadaxe is a large broad-headed axe.

name: Hatchet
summary: A hatchet (from the Old French hachete, a diminutive form of hache, 'axe' of Germanic origin) is a single-handed striking tool with a sharp blade on one side used to cut and split wood, and a hammerhead on the other side.

name: Claw hammer
summary: A claw hammer is a hammer primarily used in carpentry for driving nails into or pulling them from wood.

name: Sledgehammer
summary: A sledgehammer or sledge is a tool with a flat, massive, often metal head, attached to a long wooden or solid handle.

name: Mallet
summary: A mallet is a tool used for imparting force on another object, often made of rubber or sometimes wood, that is smaller than a maul or beetle, and usually has a relatively large head.

name: Maul
summary: A maul may refer to any number of large hammers, including:

name: Splitting wedge
summary: A wedge is a triangular shaped tool, a portable inclined plane, and one of the six simple machines.

name: Chisel
summary: A chisel is a hand tool with a characteristic wedge-shaped cutting edge on the end of its blade.

name: Gouge
summary: Gouge may refer to:

name: Centre punch
summary: A punch is a tool used to indent or create a hole through a hard surface.

name: Awl
summary: Awl may refer to:

name: Bradawl
summary: A bradawl is a woodworking hand tool with a blade similar to that of a straight screwdriver and a handle typically made from wood or plastic.

name: Handsaw
summary: In woodworking and carpentry, hand saws, also known as "panel saws", are used to cut pieces of wood into different shapes.

name: Frame saw
summary: A frame saw or sash saw is a type of saw which consists of a relatively narrow and flexible blade held under tension within a (generally wooden) rectangular frame (also called a sash or gate).

name: Bow saw
summary: A bucksaw is a metal-framed crosscut saw in the shape of a bow with a coarse wide blade generally used with a sawbuck to cut logs or firewood to length (bucking).

name: Two-man crosscut saw
summary: A crosscut saw (thwart saw) is any saw designed for cutting wood perpendicular to (across) the wood grain.

name: Hacksaw
summary: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw, originally and mainly made for cutting metal.

name: Coping saw
summary: A coping saw is a type of bow saw used to cut intricate external shapes and interior cut-outs in woodworking or carpentry.

name: Tenon saw
summary: A backsaw is any hand saw which has a stiffening rib on the edge opposite the cutting edge, enabling better control and more precise cutting than with other types of saws.

name: Wooden jack plane
summary: A hand plane is a tool for shaping wood using muscle power to force the cutting iron (blade) over the wood surface.

name: Spokeshave
summary: A spokeshave is a hand tool used to shape and smooth woods in woodworking jobs such as making cart wheel spokes, chair legs, paddles, bows, and arrows.

name: Drawknife
summary: A drawknife (drawing knife, draw shave, shaving knife) is a traditional woodworking hand tool used to shape wood by removing shavings.

name: Froe
summary: A froe (or frow), shake axe or paling knife is a tool for splitting wood by cleaving it along the grain.

name: Bow drill
summary: A bow drill is a simple hand-operated type of tool, consisting of a rod (the spindle or drill shaft) that is set in rapid rotary motion by means of a cord wrapped around it, kept taut by a bow which is pushed back and forth with one hand.

name: Brace and bit
summary: A brace is a hand tool used with a bit (drill bit or auger) to drill holes, usually in wood.

name: Auger
summary: An auger is a device to drill wood or other materials, consisting of a rotating metal shaft with a blade at the end that scrapes or cuts the wood.

name: Gimlet
summary: A gimlet is a hand tool for drilling small holes, mainly in wood, without splitting.

name: Hand drill
summary: A hand drill is the simplest primitive method to produce rapid rotary motion of a rod.

name: File
summary: A file is a tool used to remove fine amounts of material from a workpiece.

name: Rasp
summary: A rasp is a coarse form of file used for shaping wood, metal, or other material.

name: Whetstone
summary: Whetstone may refer to:

name: Grindstone
summary: A grindstone, also known as grinding stone, is a sharpening stone used for grinding or sharpening ferrous tools, used since ancient times.

name: Smith's tongs
summary: Tongs are a type of tool used to grip and lift objects, often too hot to hold, instead of holding them with the hands.

name: Anvil
summary: An anvil is a metalworking tool consisting of a large block of metal (usually forged or cast steel), with a flattened top surface, upon which another object is struck (or "worked").

name: Swage block
summary: A swage block (or swager block) is a large, heavy block of cast iron or steel used in smithing, with variously sized holes in its face and usually with forms on the sides.

name: Bellows
summary: Bellows are a device constructed to expel a controlled blast of air.

name: Bench vise
summary: A vise or vice (British English) is a mechanical apparatus used to secure an object to allow work to be performed on it.

name: Pliers
summary: Pliers are a hand tool used to hold objects firmly, possibly developed from tongs used to handle hot metal in Bronze Age Europe.

name: Pincers
summary: Pincer may refer to:

name: Spanner wrench
summary: A wrench or spanner  is a tool used to provide grip and mechanical advantage in applying torque to turn objects—usually rotary fasteners, such as nuts and bolts—or keep them from turning.

name: Monkey wrench
summary: An adjustable spanner (UK), also called a shifting spanner or shifter (Australia and New Zealand) or adjustable wrench (US and Canada), is any of various styles of spanner (wrench) with a movable jaw, allowing it to be used with different sizes of fastener head (nut, bolt, etc.) rather than just one

name: Screwdriver
summary: A  screwdriver is a tool, manual or powered, used for turning screws.

name: Crowbar
summary: A crowbar is a lever consisting of a metal bar with a single curved end and flattened points, used to force two objects apart or gain mechanical advantage in lifting; often the curved end has a notch for removing nails.

name: Pickaxe
summary: A pickaxe (American spelling: pickax), pick-axe, or pick is a generally T-shaped hand tool used for digging.

name: Mattock
summary: A mattock () is a hand tool used for digging, prying, and chopping.

name: Rock hammer
summary: A geologist's hammer, also known as rock hammer, rock pick, geological pick, or geo pick, is a specialized hammer used for splitting and breaking rocks.

name: Davy lamp
summary: The Davy lamp is a safety lamp used in flammable atmospheres, invented in 1815 by Sir Humphry Davy.

name: Hand-steel drill (jack hammer)
summary: A jackhammer (pneumatic drill, breaker, demolition hammer or road hammer in Commonwealth English) is a pneumatic or electro-mechanical tool that combines a hammer directly with a chisel.

name: Shovel
summary: A shovel is a tool used for digging, lifting, and moving bulk materials, such as soil, coal, gravel, snow, sand, or ore.

name: Spade
summary: A spade is a tool primarily for digging, consisting of a long handle and blade, typically with the blade narrower and flatter than the common shovel.

name: Garden trowel
summary: A trowel is a small hand tool used for digging, applying, smoothing, or moving small amounts of viscous or particulate material.

name: Hoe
summary: A hoe is an ancient and versatile agricultural and horticultural hand tool used to shape soil, remove weeds, clear soil, and harvest root crops.

name: Rake
summary: A rake (Old English raca, cognate with Dutch hark, German Rechen or Harke, from the root meaning 'to scrape together', 'heap up') is a broom for outside use; a versatile horticultural implement consisting of a toothed bar fixed transversely to a handle, or tines fixed to a handle, and used to collec

name: Pitchfork
summary: A pitchfork or hay fork is an agricultural tool used to pitch loose material, such as hay, straw, manure, or leaves.

name: Hay fork
summary: Hayfork may refer to:

name: Scythe
summary: A scythe (, ) is an agricultural hand-tool for mowing grass or harvesting crops.

name: Sickle
summary: A sickle, bagging hook, reaping-hook or grasshook is a single-handed agricultural tool designed with variously curved blades and typically used for harvesting or reaping grain crops, or cutting succulent forage chiefly for feeding livestock.

name: Billhook
summary: A billhook or bill hook is a versatile cutting tool used widely in agriculture and forestry for cutting woody material such as shrubs, small trees and branches.

name: Machete
summary: A machete (; Spanish pronunciation: [maˈtʃete]) is a broad blade originating from Central America.

name: Secateurs
summary: Pruning shears, also called hand pruners (in American English) or secateurs (in British English), are a type of scissors used for plants.

name: Sheep shears
summary: Shears may refer to:

name: Hedge shears
summary: A hedge trimmer, shrub trimmer, or bush trimmer is a gardening tool or machine used for trimming (cutting, pruning) hedges or solitary shrubs (bushes).

name: Wheelbarrow
summary: A wheelbarrow is a small hand-propelled load-bearing vehicle, usually with just one wheel, designed to be pushed and guided by a single person using two handles at the rear.

name: Ard plough
summary: The ard, ard plough, or scratch plough is a simple light plough without a mouldboard.

name: Moldboard plough
summary: A plough or plow (US) (both pronounced ) is a farm tool for loosening or turning soil before sowing seed or planting.

name: Harrow
summary: In agriculture, a harrow is a farm implement used for surface tillage.

name: Seed drill
summary: A seed drill is a device used in agriculture that sows seeds for crops by positioning them in the soil and burying them to a specific depth while being dragged by a tractor.

name: Threshing flail
summary: Flail may refer to:

name: Winnowing basket
summary: Winnowing is a process by which chaff is separated from grain.

name: Saddle quern
summary: A quern-stone is a stone tool for hand-grinding a wide variety of materials, especially for various types of grains.

name: Millstone
summary: Millstones or mill stones are stones used in gristmills, used for triturating, crushing or, more specifically, grinding wheat or other grains.

name: Mortar and pestle
summary: A mortar and pestle is a set of two simple tools used to prepare ingredients or substances by crushing and grinding them into a fine paste or powder in the kitchen, laboratory, and pharmacy.

name: Ox yoke
summary: A yoke is a wooden beam used between a pair of oxen or other animals to enable them to pull together on a load when working in pairs, as oxen usually do.

name: Milk pail

name: Butter churn
summary: Churn may refer to:

name: Cheese press
summary: A cheese press is a device for pressing whey from curds when making cheese.

name: Cheese mould
summary: Cheesemaking (or caseiculture) is the art of making cheese.

name: Milking stool
summary: A stool is a raised seat commonly supported by three or four legs, but with neither armrests nor a backrest.

name: Bee skep
summary: A beehive is an enclosed structure in which honey bees raise their young and produce honey as part of their seasonal cycle.

name: Bee smoker
summary: A bee smoker (usually called simply a smoker or a smokepot) is a device used in beekeeping to calm honey bees.

name: Honey extractor
summary: A honey extractor is a mechanical device used in extraction of honey from honeycombs.

name: Fishing rod
summary: A fishing rod  or fishing pole is a long, thin rod used by anglers to catch fish by manipulating a line ending in a hook (formerly known as an angle, hence the term "angling").

name: Fish hook
summary: A fish hook or fishhook, formerly also called an angle (from Old English angol and Proto-Germanic *angulaz), is a hook used to catch fish either by piercing and embedding onto the inside of the fish mouth (angling) or, more rarely, by impaling and snagging the external fish body.

name: Fishing net
summary: A fishing net or fish net is a net used for fishing.

name: Fish trap
summary: A fish trap is a trap used for catching fish and other aquatic animals of value.

name: Fishing harpoon
summary: A harpoon is a long, spear-like projectile used in fishing, whaling, sealing, and other hunting to shoot, kill, and capture large fish such as sharks or marine mammals such as seals, sea cows, and whales.

name: Lobster pot
summary: A lobster trap or lobster pot is a portable trap that traps lobsters or crayfish and is used in lobster fishing.

name: Snare trap
summary: Animal trapping, or simply trapping or ginning, is the use of a device to remotely catch and often kill an animal.

name: Tape measure
summary: A tape measure or measuring tape is a long, flexible ruler used to measure length or distance.

name: Ruler
summary: A ruler is an instrument used to make length measurements, whereby a length is read from a series of markings called "rules" along an edge of the device.

name: Set square
summary: A set square or triangle (American English) is an object used in engineering and technical drawing, with the aim of providing a straightedge at a right angle or other particular planar angle to a baseline.

name: Try square
summary: A square is a tool used for marking and referencing a 90° angle, though mitre squares are used for 45° angles.

name: Plumb bob
summary: A plumb bob, plumb bob level, or plummet, is a weight, usually with a pointed tip on the bottom, suspended from a string and used as a vertical direction as a reference line, or plumb-line.

name: Spirit level
summary: A spirit level, bubble level, or simply a level, is an instrument designed to indicate whether a surface is horizontal (level) or vertical (plumb).

name: Chalk line
summary: A chalk line or chalk box is a tool for marking long, straight lines on relatively flat surfaces, much further than is practical by hand or with a straightedge.

name: Dividers
summary: Calipers or callipers are an instrument used to measure the linear dimensions of an object or hole; namely, the length, width, thickness, diameter or depth of an object or hole.

name: Sundial
summary: A sundial is a horological device that tells the time of day (referred to as civil time in modern usage) when direct sunlight shines by the apparent position of the Sun in the sky.

name: Hourglass
summary: An hourglass (or sandglass, sand timer, or sand clock) is a device used to measure the passage of time.

name: Water clock
summary: Clepsydra may refer to:  Clepsydra, an alternative name for a water clock.

name: Balance scale
summary: A scale or balance is a device used to measure weight or mass.

name: Steelyard balance
summary: A steelyard balance, steelyard, or stilyard is a straight-beam balance with arms of unequal length.

name: Spring scale
summary: A spring scale, also known as a spring balance or newton meter, is a type of mechanical force gauge or weighing scale.

name: Magnetic compass
summary: A compass is a device that shows the cardinal directions used for navigation and geographic orientation.

name: Astrolabe
summary: An astrolabe (Ancient Greek: ἀστρολάβος, romanized: astrolábos, lit. 'star-taker'; Arabic: ٱلأَسْطُرلاب, romanized: al-Asṭurlāb; Persian: ستاره‌یاب, romanized: Setāreyāb) is an astronomical instrument dating to ancient times.

name: Sextant
summary: A sextant is a doubly reflecting navigation instrument that measures the angular distance between two visible objects.

name: Mercury thermometer
summary: A thermometer is a device that measures temperature (the hotness or coldness of an object).

name: Barometer
summary: A barometer is a scientific instrument that is used to measure air pressure.

name: Drop spindle
summary: A spindle is a straight spike, usually made from wood, used for spinning, twisting fibers such as wool, flax, hemp, and cotton into yarn.

name: Distaff
summary: A distaff (, , also called a rock) is a tool used in spinning.

name: Spinning wheel
summary: A spinning wheel is a device for spinning thread or yarn from fibres.

name: Wool comb
summary: Combing is a method for preparing carded fibre for spinning.

name: Hand cards
summary: In textile production, carding is a mechanical process that disentangles, cleans and intermixes fibres to produce a continuous web or sliver suitable for subsequent processing.

name: Niddy-noddy
summary: A niddy-noddy is a tool used to make skeins from yarn.

name: Warp-weighted loom
summary: The warp-weighted loom is a simple and ancient form of loom in which the warp yarns hang freely from a bar, which is supported by upright poles which can be placed at a convenient slant against a wall.

name: Backstrap loom
summary: A loom is a device used to weave cloth and tapestry.

name: Weaving shuttle
summary: A shuttle is a tool designed to neatly and compactly store a holder that carries the thread of the weft yarn while weaving with a loom.

name: Flying shuttle
summary: The flying shuttle or fly shuttle is a type of weaving shuttle.

name: Spinning jenny
summary: The spinning jenny is a multi-spindle spinning frame, and was one of the key developments in the industrialisation of textile manufacturing during the early Industrial Revolution.

name: Sewing needle
summary: A sewing needle, used for hand-sewing, is a long slender tool with a pointed tip at one end and a hole (or eye) to hold the sewing thread.

name: Bone needle
summary: Needle or Needles may refer to:

name: Thimble
summary: A thimble is a small pitted cup worn on the finger that protects it from being pricked or poked by a needle while sewing.

name: Sewing machine
summary: A sewing machine is a machine used to sew fabric and materials together with thread.

name: Scissors
summary: Scissors or shears are hand-operated cutting tools that consist of a pair of pivoting blades whose sharpened edges slide firmly against and past each other when the handles (shank) on the opposite side of the pivot are squeezed shut.

name: Knitting needles
summary: A knitting needle or knitting pin is a tool in hand-knitting to produce knitted fabrics.

name: Crochet hook
summary: A crochet hook is a tool used to create loops in thread or yarn and to interlock them into crochet stitches.

name: Embroidery hoop
summary: Embroidery hoops and frames are tools used to keep fabric taut while working embroidery or other forms of needlework.

name: Tatting shuttle
summary: Tatting is a technique for handcrafting a particularly durable lace from a series of knots and loops.

name: Sad iron
summary: A clothes iron, also known as a flatiron, smoothing iron, dry iron, steam iron, and simply iron, is a small appliance that, when heated, is used to press clothes to remove wrinkles and unwanted creases.

name: Dye vat
summary: Dyeing is the application of dyes or pigments on textile materials such as fibers, yarns, and fabrics with the goal of achieving color with desired color fastness.

name: Fulling stocks
summary: Fulling, also known as tucking or walking (Scots: waukin, hence often spelt waulking in Scottish English), is a step in woollen clothmaking which involves the cleansing of woven cloth (particularly wool) to eliminate (lanolin) oils, dirt, and other impurities, and to make it shrink by friction and p

name: Fleshing beam
summary: Tanning, or hide tanning, is the process of treating skins and hides of animals to produce leather.

name: Cobbler's last
summary: A last is a mechanical form used by shoemakers and cordwainers in the manufacture and repair of shoes.

name: Skinning knife
summary: The skinner knife or skinning knife is a professional tool for a skinner.

name: Hide scraper
summary: In prehistoric archaeology, scrapers are unifacial tools thought to have been used for hideworking and woodworking.

name: Flint blade
summary: In archaeology, a lithic blade is a type of stone tool created during lithic reduction by striking a long narrow flake from a stone core.

name: Stone knife
summary: A knife (pl.: knives; from Old Norse knifr 'knife, dirk') is a tool or weapon with a cutting edge or blade, usually attached to a handle or hilt.

name: Fire drill
summary: A fire drill is a method of practicing how a building should evacuate in the event of a fire or other emergencies.

name: Fire plough
summary: A fire plough (or fire plow) is a firelighting tool.

name: Flint and steel
summary: A fire striker or fire steel is a tool used in fire making, consisting of a piece of steel that can be struck against a flint, chert, or other hard rock in order to generate sparks.

name: Tinderbox
summary: A tinderbox, or patch box, is a container made of wood or metal containing flint, firesteel, and tinder (typically charcloth, but possibly a small quantity of dry, finely divided fibrous matter such as hemp), used together to help kindle a fire.

name: Friction match
summary: A match is a tool for starting a fire.

name: Pocket lighter
summary: A lighter is a portable device which uses mechanical or electrical means to create a controlled flame, and can be used to ignite a variety of flammable items, such as cigarettes,  butane gas, fireworks, candles, or campfires.

name: Tinder bracket
summary: Fomes fomentarius (commonly known as the tinder fungus, false tinder fungus, hoof fungus, tinder conk, tinder polypore or ice man fungus) is a perennial wood-decay basidiomycete found in Europe, Asia, Africa and North America.

name: Hammerstone
summary: In archaeology, a hammerstone is a hard cobble used to strike off lithic flakes from a lump of tool stone during the process of lithic reduction.

name: Pitching tool
summary: Stonemasonry, also called stonework or stonecraft, is the creation of buildings, structures, and sculpture using stone as the primary material.

name: Brick mould
summary: A brick is a type of building material used to build walls, pavements, and other elements in masonry construction.

name: Mortar tub
summary: Mortar  is a workable paste which hardens to bind building blocks such as stones, bricks, and concrete masonry units, to fill and seal the irregular gaps between them, spread the weight of them evenly, and sometimes to add decorative colours or patterns to masonry walls.

name: Pulley
summary: A pulley is a wheel on an axle or shaft enabling a taut cable or belt passing over the wheel to move and change direction, or transfer power between itself and a shaft.

name: Block and tackle
summary: A block and tackle, purchase, or only tackle is a system of two or more pulleys with a rope or cable threaded between them, used to provide tension and lift heavy loads.

name: Winch
summary: A winch is a mechanical device that is used to pull in (wind up) or let out (wind out) or otherwise adjust the tension of a rope or wire rope (also called "cable" or "wire cable").

name: Windlass
summary: The windlass  is a type of horizontal winch used to move heavy weights, featuring a cylinder (barrel) operated by a crank to wind a rope.

name: Capstan
summary: A capstan is a vertical-axled rotating machine developed for use on sailing ships to multiply the pulling force of sailors when hauling ropes, cables, and hawsers.

name: Lever
summary: A lever is a simple machine consisting of a beam or rigid rod pivoted at a fixed hinge or fulcrum.

name: Twisted rope
summary: A rope is a group of yarns, plies, fibres, or strands that are twisted or braided together into a larger and stronger form.

name: Ladder
summary: A ladder is a vertical or inclined set of rungs or steps commonly used for climbing or descending.

name: Grappling hook
summary: A grappling hook, or grapnel, is a drag-looking device intended for grappling onto something.

name: Iron shackle
summary: A shackle (or shacklebolt), also known as a gyve, is a U-shaped piece of metal secured with a clevis pin or bolt across the opening, or a hinged metal loop secured with a quick-release locking pin mechanism.

name: Iron chain
summary: A chain is a serial assembly of connected links typically made of metal, with an overall character similar to that of a rope in that it is flexible and curved in compression, but linear, rigid, and load-bearing in tension.

name: Padlock
summary: Padlocks are portable locks with a shackle that may be passed through an opening (such as a chain link, or hasp staple) to prevent use, theft, vandalism or harm.

name: Door key
summary: A lock is a mechanical or electronic fastening device that is released by a physical object (such as a key, keycard, fingerprint, RFID card, security token or coin), by supplying secret information (such as a number or letter permutation or password), by a combination thereof, or it may only be able

name: Pin tumbler lock
summary: The pin tumbler lock, also known as the Yale lock (after Linus Yale Jr) is a lock mechanism that uses a series of spring-loaded pins of varying lengths to prevent the lock from opening without the correct key.

name: Lever lock
summary: A lever tumbler lock is a type of lock whose mechanism uses a set of levers to prevent the bolt from moving in the lock.

name: Door hinge
summary: A hinge is a mechanical bearing that connects two solid objects, typically allowing only a limited angle of rotation between them.

name: Iron nail
summary: In woodworking and construction, a nail is a small object made of metal (or wood, called a tree nail or "trunnel") which is used as a fastener, as a peg to hang something, or sometimes as a decoration.

name: Wood screw
summary: A screw is an externally helical threaded fastener capable of being tightened or released by a twisting force (torque) to the head.

name: Nut and bolt
summary: A bolt is an externally helical threaded fastener capable of being tightened or released by a twisting force (torque) to a matching nut.

name: Rivet
summary: A rivet is a semi permanent mechanical fastener.

name: Glue pot
summary: Animal glue is an adhesive that is created by prolonged boiling of animal connective tissue in a process called rendering.

name: Clamp
summary: A clamp is a fastening device used to hold or secure objects tightly together to prevent movement or separation through the application of inward pressure.

name: Sawhorse
summary: In woodworking, a saw-horse or sawhorse (saw-buck, trestle, buck) is a trestle structure used to support a board or plank for sawing.

name: Workbench
summary: A workbench is a sturdy table at which manual work is done.

name: Pole lathe
summary: A lathe () is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis of rotation to perform various operations such as cutting, sanding, knurling, drilling, deformation, facing, threading and turning, with tools that are applied to the workpiece to create an object with symmetry about that axis.

name: Wood turning gouge
summary: Woodturning is the craft of using a wood lathe with hand-held tools to cut a shape that is symmetrical around the axis of rotation.

name: Cooper's adze
summary: A cooper is a craftsman who produces wooden casks, barrels, vats, buckets, tubs, troughs, and other similar containers from timber staves that were usually heated or steamed to make them pliable.

name: Barrel hoop driver
summary: A barrel or cask is a hollow cylindrical container with a bulging center, longer than it is wide.

name: Spoked wheel
summary: A wheel is a rotating component (typically circular in shape) intended to turn on an axle bearing.

name: Grease pot
summary: Grease is a solid or semisolid lubricant formed as a dispersion of thickening agents in a liquid lubricant.

name: Wooden bucket
summary: A bucket is typically a watertight, vertical cylinder or truncated cone or square, with an open top and a flat bottom that is attached to a semicircular carrying handle called the bail.

name: Well bucket and windlass
summary: A well is an excavation or structure created on the earth by digging, driving, or drilling to access liquid resources, usually water.

name: Funnel
summary: A funnel is a tube or pipe that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, used for guiding liquid or powder into a small opening.

name: Dipper
summary: A ladle is a large, deep spoon, often used in the preparation and serving of soup, stew, or other foods.

name: Oil can
summary: An oil can (oilcan or oiler) is a can that holds oil (usually motor oil) for lubricating machines.

name: Grease gun
summary: A grease gun is a common workshop and garage tool used for lubrication.

name: Hand pump
summary: A pump is a device that moves fluids (liquids or gases), or sometimes slurries, by mechanical action, typically converted from electrical energy into hydraulic or pneumatic energy.

name: Archimedes' screw
summary: An Archimedes' screw is a hydraulic machine composed of an outer cylinder and an inner cylinder with helical blades.

name: Shaduf
summary: A shadoof (or shaduf, well pole, well sweep, sweep, swape, or simply a lift) is a tool that is used to lift water from a well or another water source onto land or into another waterway or basin.

name: Noria
summary: A noria (Arabic: ناعورة, romanized: nā‘ūra) is a hydropowered scoop wheel used to lift water into a small aqueduct, either for the purpose of irrigation or to supply water to cities and villages.

name: Watering can
summary: A watering can (or watering pot or watering jug) is a portable container, usually with a handle and a funnel, used to water plants by hand.

name: Cooking pot
summary: A cooking pot (saucepan in British English) is a large bowl that is heated in order to cook the food inside it.

name: Cauldron
summary: A cauldron (or a caldron) is a large pot or kettle used for cooking or boiling, typically over an open fire.

name: Dutch oven
summary: A Dutch oven, Dutch pot (US English), or casserole dish (international) is a thick-walled cooking pot with a tight-fitting lid.

name: Frying pan
summary: A frying pan, also called frypan or skillet, is a flat-bottomed cookware used for frying, searing and browning foods.

name: Wok
summary: A wok (simplified Chinese: 镬; traditional Chinese: 鑊; pinyin: huò; Cantonese Yale: wohk) is a deep round-bottomed cooking pan of either indigenous Chinese origin or derived from the South Asian karahi.

name: Saucepan

summary: A breadbox (chiefly American) or a breadbin (chiefly British) is a container for storing bread and other baked goods to keep them fresh.

name: Icebox
summary: An icebox (also called a cold closet) is a compact, non-mechanical refrigerator which was a common early-twentieth-century kitchen appliance before the development of safely powered refrigeration devices.

name: Root bin
summary: A root cellar (American and Canadian English), fruit cellar (Mid-Western American English) or earth cellar (British English) is a structure, usually underground or partially underground, used for storage of vegetables, fruits, nuts, or other foods.

name: Besom broom
summary: A broom (), also known as a broomstick, is a cleaning tool, consisting of usually stiff fibers (often made of materials such as plastic, glued hair, or corn husks) attached to, and roughly parallel to, a cylindrical handle, the broomstick.

name: Dustpan
summary: A dustpan, the small version of which is also known as a "hearth brush and shovel” (from its use of cleaning the fireplace hearth), is a cleaning utensil.

name: Mop
summary: A mop (such as a floor mop) is a mass or bundle of coarse strings or yarn, etc., or a piece of cloth, sponge or other absorbent material, attached to a pole or stick.

name: Scrub brush
summary: A brush is a common tool with bristles, wire, or other filaments.

name: Laundry beetle
summary: Laundry is the washing of clothing and other textiles, and, more broadly, their drying and ironing as well.

name: Hand mangle
summary: A mangle is a mechanical laundry aid consisting of two rollers in a sturdy frame, connected by cogs and, in its home version, powered by a hand crank or by electricity.

name: Clothes peg
summary: A clothespin (US English) or clothes peg (UK English), also spelled "clothes pin"  is a fastener used to hang up clothes for drying, usually on a clothes line.

name: Clothes line
summary: A clothes line, also spelled clothesline, also known as a wash line, is a device for hanging clothes on for the purpose of drying or airing out the articles.

name: Soap bar
summary: Soap is a salt of a fatty acid (sometimes other carboxylic acids) used for cleaning and lubricating products as well as other applications.

name: Chamber pot
summary: A chamber pot is a portable toilet, meant for nocturnal use in the bedroom.

name: Bed warming pan
summary: A bed warmer or warming pan was a common household item in countries with cold winters, especially in Europe.

name: Hot water bottle
summary: A hot-water bottle is a bottle filled with hot water and sealed with a stopper, used to provide warmth, typically while in bed, but also for the application of heat to a specific part of the body.

name: Hand fan
summary: A handheld fan, or simply hand fan, is a broad, flat surface that is waved back and forth to create an airflow.

name: Umbrella
summary: An umbrella (parasol or rarely parapluie) is a folding canopy supported by wooden or metal ribs that is mounted on a wooden, metal, or plastic pole.

name: Bronze hand mirror
summary: A mirror, also known as a looking glass, is an object that reflects an image.

name: Comb
summary: A comb is a tool consisting of a shaft that holds a row of teeth for pulling through the hair to clean, untangle, or style it.

name: Hairbrush
summary: A hairbrush is a brush with rigid (hard or inflexible) or light and soft spokes used in hair care for smoothing, styling, and detangling human hair, or for grooming an animal's fur.

name: Straight razor
summary: A razor is a bladed tool primarily used in the removal of body hair through the act of shaving.

name: Tweezers
summary: Tweezers are small hand tools used for grasping objects too small to be easily handled with the human fingers.

name: Toothbrush
summary: A toothbrush is a special type of brush used to clean the teeth, gums, and tongue.

name: Nail clippers
summary: A nail clipper (also called nail clippers, a nail trimmer, a nail cutter or nipper type) is a hand tool used to trim nails and hangnails.

name: Wooden chair
summary: A chair (/t͡ʃɛɚ/ ) is a type of seat, typically designed for one person and consisting of one or more legs, a flat or slightly angled seat, and a back rest.

name: Three-legged stool

name: Bench
summary: A bench is a long seat on which several people may sit at the same time.

name: Wooden table
summary: A table is a piece of furniture with a raised flat top and is supported most commonly by 1 to 4 legs (although some can have more).

name: Bed frame
summary: A bed is a piece of furniture that is used as a place to sleep, rest, and relax.

name: Cradle

name: Bookshelf
summary: A bookcase also called a bookshelf, is a piece of furniture with horizontal shelves, often in a cabinet, used to store books or other printed materials.

name: Cupboard
summary: A cupboard is a piece of furniture for enclosing dishware or grocery items that are stored in a home.

name: Wardrobe
summary: A wardrobe, also called armoire or almirah, is a piece of standing furniture used for storing clothes.

name: Fire shovel
summary: A fireplace or hearth is a structure made of brick, stone or metal designed to contain a fire.

name: Tinder pouch
summary: Tinder is easily combustible material used to start a fire.

name: Coal scuttle
summary: A coal scuttle, sometimes spelled coalscuttle and also called a hod, "coal bucket", or "coal pail", is a bucket-like container for holding a small, intermediate supply of coal convenient to an indoor coal-fired stove or heater.

name: Cast iron stove
summary: A stove or range is an appliance or construction that generates heat inside or atop the device using an energy source.

name: Pot-bellied stove
summary: A potbelly stove is a cast-iron, coal-burning or wood-burning stove that is cylindrical with a bulge in the middle.

name: Kang bed-stove
summary: The kang (Chinese: 炕; pinyin: kàng; Manchu: ᠨᠠᡥᠠᠨ nahan, Kazakh: кән) is a traditional heated platform, 2 metres or more long, used for general living, working, entertaining and sleeping in the northern part of China, where the winter climate is cold.

name: Brazier
summary: A brazier () is a container used to burn charcoal or other solid fuel for cooking, heating, and/or rituals.

name: Kotatsu
summary: A kotatsu (Japanese: 炬燵 or こたつ) is a low, wooden table frame covered by a futon, or heavy blanket, upon which a table top sits.

name: Quill pen
summary: A quill is a writing tool made from a moulted flight feather of a large bird.

name: Reed pen
summary: A reed pen (Ancient Greek: κάλαμοι kalamoi; singular κάλαμος kalamos) or bamboo pen (traditional Chinese: 竹筆; simplified Chinese: 竹笔; pinyin: zhú bǐ) is a writing implement made by cutting and shaping a single reed straw or length of bamboo.

name: Stylus
summary: A stylus is a writing implement or tool for scribing or marking into softer materials.

name: Wax tablet
summary: A wax tablet is a tablet made of wood and covered with a layer of wax, often linked loosely to a cover tablet, as a "double-leaved"  diptych.

name: Calligraphy brush
summary: Chinese calligraphy is the writing of Chinese characters as an art form, combining visual art and interpretation of their literary meaning.

name: Inkwell
summary: An inkwell is a small jar or container, often made of glass, porcelain, silver, brass, or pewter, used for holding ink in a place convenient for the person who is writing.

name: Ink stick
summary: Inksticks (Chinese: 墨; pinyin: ) or ink cakes are a type of solid Chinese ink used traditionally in several Chinese, Japanese, and East Asian art forms such as calligraphy and brush painting.

name: Inkstone
summary: An inkstone is a stone mortar for the grinding and containment of ink.

name: Steel nib pen
summary: A dip pen is a writing instrument used to apply ink to paper by dipping into an inkwell.

name: Fountain pen
summary: A fountain pen is a writing instrument that uses a metal nib to apply water-based ink to paper.

name: Pencil
summary: A pencil ( ) is a writing or drawing implement with a solid pigment core in a protective casing that reduces the risk of core breakage and keeps it from marking the user's hand.

name: Seal stamp
summary: A seal is a device for making an impression in wax, clay, paper, or some other medium, including an embossment on paper, and is also the impression thus made.

name: Papyrus scroll
summary: Papyrus ( pə-PY-rəs) is a substance used in ancient times as a writing surface.

name: Abacus
summary: An abacus (pl.

name: Slide rule
summary: A slide rule is a hand-operated mechanical calculator consisting of slidable rulers for conducting mathematical operations such as multiplication, division, exponents, roots, logarithms, and trigonometry.

name: Printing press
summary: A printing press is a machine that applies pressure to transfer ink onto a surface made of paper, cloth, or a similar material.

name: Typewriter
summary: A typewriter is a mechanical or electromechanical machine for typing characters.

name: Potter's wheel
summary: In pottery, a potter's wheel is a machine used in the shaping (known as throwing) of clay into round ceramic ware.

name: Paddle and anvil
summary: Pottery is the process and the products of forming vessels and other objects with clay and other raw materials, which are fired at high temperatures to give them a hard and durable form.

name: Updraft kiln
summary: A kiln is a thermally insulated chamber, a type of oven, that produces temperatures sufficient to complete some process, such as hardening, drying, or chemical changes.

name: Blowpipe
summary: Glassblowing is a glassforming technique that involves inflating molten glass into a bubble (or parison) with the aid of a blowpipe (or blow tube).

name: Crucible
summary: A crucible is a container in which metals or other substances are melted or subjected to very high temperatures.

name: Ingot mould
summary: An ingot is a piece of relatively pure material, usually metal, that is cast into a shape suitable for further processing.

name: Casting ladle
summary: A foundry is a factory that produces metal castings.

name: Cross-peen hammer
summary: A ball-peen (also ball-pein) or machinist's hammer is a type of peening hammer used in metalworking.

name: Trip hammer
summary: A trip hammer, also known as a tilt hammer or helve hammer, is a massive powered hammer, usually raised by a cam and then released to fall under the force of gravity.

name: Draw plate
summary: Wire drawing is a metalworking process used to reduce the cross-section of a wire by pulling the wire through one or more dies.

name: Jeweller's saw
summary: A piercing saw, also known as a jeweler's saw or jeweler's blade, is a type of saw commonly used in jewelry making on sheet metal.

name: Horseshoe
summary: A horseshoe is a piece of equestrian equipment that protects a horse hoof from wear.

name: Farrier's rasp
summary: A farrier is a specialist in farriery: equine hoof care, including the trimming and balancing of horses' hooves and the placing of shoes on their hooves when necessary.

name: Hoof pick
summary: Horse grooming is hygienic care given to a horse, or a process by which the horse's physical appearance is enhanced for horse shows or other types of competition.

name: Saddle
summary: A saddle is a supportive structure for a rider of an animal, fastened to an animal's back by a girth.

name: Stirrup
summary: A stirrup is one of a pair of light frames or rings attached to the saddle of a riding animal (usually a horse or other equine, such as a mule) by a strap (often called a stirrup leather) that holds its rider's foot, aiding in their mounting and support.

name: Bridle
summary: A bridle is a piece of equipment used to direct a horse.

name: Halter
summary: A halter or headcollar is headgear placed on animals used to lead or tie up livestock and, occasionally, other animals; it fits behind the ears (behind the poll), and around the muzzle.

name: Cowbell
summary: A cowbell (or cow bell) is a bell worn around the neck of free-roaming livestock so herders can keep track of an animal via the sound of the bell when the animal is grazing out of view in hilly landscapes or vast plains.

name: Hand bell
summary: A handbell is a bell designed to be rung by hand.

name: Gong
summary: A gong is a percussion instrument originating from Southeast Asia, and used widely in Southeast Asian and East Asian musical traditions.
